translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou he was transferred to Investigating and Transport Commissioner of the Shandong East and West Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou he became Investigating and Transport Commissioner of the Shandong East and West Route.

sentences.zh: 是歲按察司罷，仍充轉運使。

translations.literal: That year the Investigation Commission was abolished; he still served as Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Investigation Commission was abolished; he remained Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，致仕。

translations.literal: After some time he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired.

sentences.zh: 興定二年十一月庚辰，宣宗禦登賢門，召致仕官，兵部尚書完顏蒲剌都、戶部尚書蕭貢、刑部尚書僕散偉、工部尚書奧屯紮裏吉、翰林學士完顏孛迭、轉運使福僧、河東北路轉運使趙重福、沁南軍節度使豬奮、鎮南軍節度使石抹仲溫、泰定軍節度使李元輔、中衛尉完顏奴婢、原州刺史紇石烈孛吉賜食，訪問時政得失。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the eleventh month of the second year of Xingding, the Xuanzong Emperor held court at the Dengxian Gate, summoned retired officials—Minister of War Wanyan Puladu, Minister of Revenue Xiao Gong, Minister of Punishments Pusan Wei, Minister of Works Aotun Zhali, Hanlin Academician Wanyan Biedie, Transport Commissioner Fuseng, Hedong North Route Transport Commissioner Zhao Chongfu, Military Commissioner of the Qinnan Army Zhu Fen, Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army Shimozhong Wen, Military Commissioner of the Taiding Army Li Yuanfu, Commandant of the Central Guard Wanyan Nubi, and Prefect of Yuanzhou Geshilie Boji—gave them food, and inquired into the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the eleventh month of the second year of Xingding, the Xuanzong Emperor held court at Dengxian Gate, summoned retired officials including Ministers Puladu, Xiao Gong, Pusan Wei, Aotun Zhali, Hanlin Academician Biedie, Transport Commissioner Fuseng, Zhao Chongfu, Zhu Fen, Shimozhong Wen, Li Yuanfu, Commandant Nubi, and Prefect Boji, feasted them, and asked what policy had gained or lost.

sentences.zh: 福僧乃上書曰：「為今之計，惟先招徠颭人。

translations.literal: Fuseng then submitted a memorial: "For the present plan, only first win over the Shan people.
translations.idiomatic: Fuseng memorialized: "Today's strategy must begin by winning over the Shan people.

sentences.zh: 選擇颭人舊有宿望雄辨者，諭以恩信，彼若內附，然後中都可複，遼東可通。

translations.literal: Choose among the Shan those of old standing and eloquence, instruct them with grace and trust; if they submit inward, then the central capital can be recovered and Liaodong reopened.
translations.idiomatic: Choose Shan leaders of old standing and eloquence, win them with grace and trust; if they come in, Zhongdu can be recovered and Liaodong reopened.

sentences.zh: 今西北多虞，而南鄙不敢撤戍，芻糧調度，仰給河南，賦役頻繁，民力疲弊。

translations.literal: Now the northwest has many alarms while the southern marches dare not withdraw garrisons; fodder and grain are supplied from Henan, levies are frequent, and the people's strength is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest is troubled yet the south cannot strip garrisons; fodder and grain depend on Henan, levies multiply, and the people are spent.

sentences.zh: 宜開宋人講和之端，撫定河朔，養兵蓄銳，策之上也。」

translations.literal: One should open talks for peace with Song, pacify Hebei, rest the troops and store strength—that is the superior policy."
translations.idiomatic: Open peace talks with Song, pacify Hebei, rest troops and store strength—that is the best policy."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「山東殘破，群盜滿野，官軍既少，且無騎兵。

translations.literal: He also said: "Shandong is ruined, bandits fill the countryside, government troops are few and there is no cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Shandong lies in ruins, bandits cover the fields, government troops are few, and there is no cavalry.

sentences.zh: 若宋人資以糧餉，假以官爵，為患愈大。

translations.literal: If Song supplies them grain and fodder and lends them offices and ranks, the harm will be still greater.
translations.idiomatic: If Song feeds them and grants titles, the harm grows worse.

sentences.zh: 當選才幹官充宣差招捕，以恩賞諭使複業。

translations.literal: Able officials should be chosen as special commissioners to recruit and suppress, using grace and rewards to urge them back to their trades.
translations.idiomatic: Send able commissioners to recruit and pacify, using grace and rewards to restore livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 募其壯悍為兵，亦致勝之一也。」

translations.literal: Recruit their stalwart and fierce as soldiers—this too is one way to win."
translations.idiomatic: Recruit the bold among them as soldiers—another path to victory."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自承安用兵，軍中設監戰官，論議之間，動相矛盾，不懲其失，反以為法。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since troops were used in Cheng'an, battle supervisors were set up in the army; in discussion they constantly contradict one another, their failures are not punished, and this is taken as law.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Since Cheng'an, armies have carried battle supervisors who contradict commanders in council, suffer no penalty for failure, and yet set precedent.

sentences.zh: 若輩平居，皆選材勇自衛，一旦有急，驅疲懦出戰，寧不敗事？

translations.literal: Such men in peace all choose the talented and brave to guard themselves; once there is urgency they drive the weary and cowardly into battle—will they not ruin affairs?
translations.idiomatic: In peace they surround themselves with the brave; in crisis they send the weak to fight—how can that succeed?

sentences.zh: 罷之為便。」

translations.literal: Abolishing them would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Abolish them."

sentences.zh: 書奏，朝廷略施用焉。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and the court adopted it in part.
translations.idiomatic: The court received the memorial and adopted parts of it.

sentences.zh: 元光元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yuanguang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宣宗急於求賢，而使小人間之；

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Xuanzong Emperor was eager to seek the worthy, yet let petty men come between;
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The Xuanzong Emperor sought worthies urgently, yet petty men came between him and them;

sentences.zh: 悅于直言，而使邪說亂之。

translations.literal: he delighted in straight speech, yet let perverse doctrines confuse it.
translations.idiomatic: he welcomed blunt speech, yet perverse doctrines confused it.

sentences.zh: 貞祐、興定之間，豈無其人哉。

translations.literal: Between Zhenyou and Xingding, were there truly no such men?
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhenyou and Xingding, were there truly no such men?

sentences.zh: 雖故直言蔽於所惑，群才詘於見忌耳。

translations.literal: Though the old blunt speakers were blocked by what deluded them, the host of talents were bent by being envied.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt speakers were blinded by their own fixations; many talents were crushed by envy.

sentences.zh: 自納坦謀嘉以下，可考見焉。

translations.literal: From Natan Moujia downward, this may be examined.
translations.idiomatic: From Natan Moujia onward, this can be seen in these lives.

sentences.zh: 奧屯忠孝

translations.literal: Aotun Zhongxiao
translations.idiomatic: Aotun Zhongxiao

sentences.zh: 奧屯忠孝，字全道，本名牙哥，懿州胡土虎猛安人。

translations.literal: Aotun Zhongxiao, style name Quandao, original name Yage, was a native of Hutuhu Meng'an in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Aotun Zhongxiao, courtesy name Quandao, born Yage, came from Hutuhu Meng'an in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was filial to his mother.

sentences.zh: 中大定二十二年進士科，調蒲州司候，察廉，遷一官，除校書郎兼太子司經。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Dading he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Postal Station Officer of Puzhou, selected in an integrity review and promoted one rank, made Collator with concurrent Master of Classics for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-second year of Dading, became Postal Station Officer of Puzhou, won promotion in an integrity review, and served as Collator and Master of Classics for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose three ranks to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林待制，權戶部侍郎，佐參知政事胥持國治決河，以勞進一階。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, acted as Vice Minister of Revenue, and assisted Vice Councilor Xu Chiguo in managing the Yellow River breach, advancing one rank for labor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, acted as Vice Minister of Revenue, helped Vice Councilor Xu Chiguo seal the Yellow River breach, and advanced one rank for the labor.

sentences.zh: 除河平軍節度使，兼都水監，遂疏七祖佛河及王村、周平、道口、雞爪、孫家港，複開東明、南陽岡、馬蹄、孫村諸河。

translations.literal: He was made Military Commissioner of the Heping Army with concurrent directorship of the Directorate of Waterways, and dredged the Qizu Buddha River and Wangcun, Zhouping, Daokou, Jizhua, and Sunjia harbors, reopening the Dongming, Nanyanggang, Mati, and Suncun rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He became Military Commissioner of the Heping Army and Director of Waterways, dredging the Qizu Buddha River and the Wangcun, Zhouping, Daokou, Jizhua, and Sunjia channels, reopening the Dongming, Nanyanggang, Mati, and Suncun rivers.

sentences.zh: 忠孝常曰：「河之為患，不免勞民。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao often said: "The river's harm cannot avoid troubling the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiao often said: "River work cannot spare the people labor.

sentences.zh: 複壘石為岸十餘裏，民不勝其病矣。」

translations.literal: Restoring stone embankments for more than ten li, the people could not bear the affliction."
translations.idiomatic: Rebuilding stone banks for more than ten li crushed the people."

sentences.zh: 改沁南軍，坐前在衛州勾集妨農軍借民錢不令償，由是貧富不相假貸，軍民不相安，降甯海州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Qinnan Army; because while previously in Weizhou he had gathered people and hindered farming, and army loans of commoners' money were not repaid, rich and poor would not lend to one another and soldiers and people were unsettled, he was demoted to Prefect of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to the Qinnan Army, he was demoted to Prefect of Ninghai for earlier abuses in Weizhou—pressing farmers, collecting army loans without repayment, and unsettling soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 改滑州，曆同知南京留守，遷定國軍節度使，複為沁南軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Huazhou, served as Associate Defender of Nanjing, transferred to Military Commissioner of the Dingguo Army, and again to the Qinnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Huazhou, served as Associate Defender of Nanjing, became Military Commissioner of the Dingguo Army, then returned to the Qinnan Army.

sentences.zh: 入為太子少傅兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered service as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with concurrent appointment as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，議降衛紹王，忠孝與蒲察思忠附胡沙虎議，語在思忠傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, when deposing Prince Shao of Wei, Zhongxiao and Pucha Sizhong sided with Hushahu—the account is in Sizhong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou, when Prince Shao of Wei was deposed, Zhongxiao and Pucha Sizhong backed Hushahu—as told in Sizhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Vice Councilor.

sentences.zh: 中都圍急，糧運道絕，詔忠孝搜括民間積粟，存兩月食用，悉令輸官，酬以銀鈔或僧道戒牒。

translations.literal: When Zhongdu was besieged in grave peril and grain transport routes were cut, an edict ordered Zhongxiao to search out grain the people had stored privately, enough for two months' food, and have it all delivered to the government, repaid with silver notes or Buddhist or Daoist ordination certificates.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongdu was besieged and supply routes cut, the court ordered Zhongxiao to seize private grain stores—two months' food—paying in silver notes or ordination certificates.

sentences.zh: 是時，知大興府事胥鼎計畫軍食，奏許人納粟買官，鼎已籍者，忠孝再括之，令百姓兩輸，欲為己功。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Ding, Administrator of Daxing Prefecture, was planning army provisions and memorialized allowing people to buy office with grain; those Ding had registered Zhongxiao searched again, making the people pay twice so he could claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ding, Administrator of Daxing, allowed grain purchases of office; Zhongxiao re-seized grain Ding had already registered, forcing double payment to claim credit.

sentences.zh: 左諫議大夫張行信上疏論之曰：「民食止存兩月，而又奪之，使當絕食，不獨歸咎有司，而亦怨朝廷之不察也。」

translations.literal: Left Remonstrator Zhang Xingxin submitted a memorial: "The people's food lasts only two months, yet it is seized again; when they must starve, blame will fall not only on officials but on the court's failure to see clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrator Zhang Xingxin said: "People hold only two months' grain, yet it is seized again; when they starve, blame will fall on the court as well as officials."

sentences.zh: 宣宗善行信言，命近臣與忠孝同審取焉。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor followed Xingxin's words and ordered close officials to review with Zhongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor heeded Zhang and ordered close officials to review with Zhongxiao.

sentences.zh: 謂忠孝曰：「國家本欲得糧，今既得矣，姑從民便可也。」

translations.literal: He told Zhongxiao: "The state originally wished to obtain grain; now that it has been obtained, for the time being follow what is convenient for the people."
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhongxiao: "We wanted grain; now we have it—let the people keep what ease we can grant."

sentences.zh: 頃之，行信複奏曰：「參政奧屯忠孝平生矯偽不近人情，急於功名，詭異要譽，慘刻害物，忍而不恤。

translations.literal: Shortly Xingxin again memorialized: "Vice Councilor Aotun Zhongxiao has all his life been falsely upright and estranged from human feeling, eager for fame, using strangeness to seek praise, cruel and harmful to things, ruthless and unsparing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang memorialized again: "Vice Councilor Aotun Zhongxiao is falsely upright, hungry for fame, cruel to people, and pitiless.

sentences.zh: 勾當河防，河朔居民不勝其病。

translations.literal: While managing river defense, the people of Hebei could not bear the affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Managing river works, he broke the people of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 軍負民錢，抑不令償。

translations.literal: The army owed the people's money and he suppressed repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Army debts to civilians went unpaid by his order.

sentences.zh: 東海欲用胡沙虎，舉朝皆曰不可，忠孝獨力薦。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace wished to use Hushahu; the whole court said it could not be done, but Zhongxiao alone urged it strongly.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace wanted Hushahu; the court opposed it, but Zhongxiao alone urged him strongly.

sentences.zh: 及胡沙虎作難，忠孝自謂有功。

translations.literal: When Hushahu made trouble Zhongxiao considered himself meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: When Hushahu rebelled, Zhongxiao claimed merit.

sentences.zh: 詔議東海爵號，忠孝請籍沒其子孫，及論特末也則雲不當籍沒，其偏黨不公如此。

translations.literal: When an edict discussed the Eastern Palace's title, Zhongxiao asked to confiscate his descendants' property, yet when Temode was discussed he said confiscation should not apply—his partiality was so unfair.
translations.idiomatic: Debating the Eastern Palace's title he demanded confiscation of descendants' property; on Temode he opposed confiscation—so partial was he.

sentences.zh: 無事之時，猶不容一相非才，況今多故，乃使此人與政，如社稷何！」

translations.literal: In peaceful times he could not tolerate one unfit chancellor; how much less in many emergencies—what of the altars if such a man holds power!"
translations.idiomatic: In peace he could not bear one unfit minister; in crisis, what becomes of the state if he governs?"

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「朕初即位，當以禮進退大臣，卿語其親知，諷之求去可也。」

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor said: "When I first took the throne I should advance and retire great ministers by ritual; tell those close to him to hint that he should seek to leave."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have just taken the throne and must retire ministers with ritual; tell his friends to hint he should resign."

sentences.zh: 行信以語右司郎中把胡魯，把胡魯以宣宗意白忠孝，忠孝塤然不聽。

translations.literal: Xingxin told Right Department Director Bahuru; Bahuru told Zhongxiao the emperor's intent, but Zhongxiao was unmoved and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang told Bahuru, who relayed the emperor's wish; Zhongxiao ignored it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，罷為太子太保，出知濟南府事，改知中山府。

translations.literal: Shortly he was dismissed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and sent out to govern Jinan Prefecture, then changed to govern Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was dismissed as Junior Tutor and sent to govern Jinan, then Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，年七十，諡惠敏。

translations.literal: Before long he died at seventy and was given the posthumous title Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy and received the posthumous title Huimin.

sentences.zh: 蒲察思忠

translations.literal: Pucha Sizhong
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Sizhong

sentences.zh: 蒲察思忠，本名畏也，隆安路合懶合兀主猛安人。

translations.literal: Pucha Sizhong, original name Weiye, was a native of Helan Hewuzhu Meng'an in Long'an Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Sizhong, born Weiye, came from Helan Hewuzhu Meng'an in Long'an Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定二十五年進士，調文德、漷陰主簿，國子助教，應奉翰林文字，太學博士，累遷涿州刺史，吏部郎中，遷潞王傅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk at Wende and Huoyin, National University assistant instructor, Hanlin Academician for Service, National University erudite, and rose through posts to Prefect of Zhuo, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Tutor of the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, served as chief clerk at Wende and Huoyin, National University assistant, Hanlin Academician for Service, National University erudite, then Prefect of Zhuo, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Tutor of the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 被詔與翰林侍讀學士張行簡討論武成王廟配等列，思忠奏曰：「伏見武成王廟配享諸將，不以世代為先。

translations.literal: By imperial order he joined Hanlin Academician for Lectures Zhang Xingjian in discussing the ranking of associates in the temple of King Wu of Cheng; Sizhong memorialized: "I observe that in the temple of King Wu of Cheng the generals honored in sacrifice are not ordered by generation.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Hanlin Academician Zhang Xingjian to rank King Wu of Cheng's temple associates, Sizhong said: "The honored generals there are not arranged by era.

sentences.zh: 後按唐祀典，李靖、李勣居吳起、樂毅上。

translations.literal: Later, according to Tang sacrificial regulations, Li Jing and Li Ji rank above Wu Qi and Yue Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang ritual places Li Jing and Li Ji above Wu Qi and Yue Yi.

sentences.zh: 聖朝太祖以二千之眾，破百萬之師，太宗克宋，成此帝業，秦王宗翰、宋王宗望、婁室、穀神與前代之將，各以功德間列可也。」

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Taizu with two thousand men broke an army of a million; Taizong conquered Song and accomplished this imperial enterprise. Prince Zonghan of Qin, Prince Zongwang of Song, Wushi, and Gushen may each, with the generals of former ages, be ranked by merit in turn."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu broke a million-man host with two thousand men; Taizong conquered Song and built the empire. Prince Zonghan, Prince Zongwang, Wushi, and Gushen may stand with past generals, each honored for merit."

sentences.zh: 思忠論多矯飾，不盡錄，錄其頗有理者雲。

translations.literal: Sizhong's arguments were much adorned and are not fully recorded; what was rather reasonable is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong's arguments were often overwrought and are not fully recorded; only what was reasonably argued is kept here.

sentences.zh: 遷大理卿，兼左司諫，同修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Justice with concurrent Left Remonstrator and Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chief Justice, Left Remonstrator, and Compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，平章政事僕散揆宣撫河南，詔以備禦攻守之法，集百官議於尚書省。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, Councilor Pusan Kui pacified Henan; an edict sought methods of defense for attack and holding, and all officials were assembled to deliberate in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe, Councilor Pusan Kui pacified Henan; the court sought defensive methods and gathered officials in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 廷臣尚多異議，思忠曰：「宋人攻圍城邑，動至數千，不得為小寇。

translations.literal: Court ministers still mostly disagreed; Sizhong said: "When Song men besiege cities and towns they often number thousands and cannot be called small bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers still disagreed; Sizhong said: "Song forces besieging towns number thousands—they are no petty raid.

sentences.zh: 但當選擇賢將，宜攻宜守，臨時制變，無不可者。」

translations.literal: Only choose worthy generals fit to attack or defend and adapt to the moment—nothing is impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy generals who can attack or hold and adapt in the moment—nothing is impossible."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷翰林侍講學士兼左諫議大夫，大理卿、同修國史如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Hanlin Academician for Lectures with concurrent Left Remonstrator, keeping Chief Justice and Compiler of the National History as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Hanlin Academician for Lectures and Left Remonstrator, retaining Chief Justice and national history duties.

sentences.zh: 再閱月，兼知審官院正職，外兼四職自思忠始。

translations.literal: After another month he concurrently managed the Bureau of Review as regular post; holding four outside posts together began with Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he also ran the Bureau of Review in regular capacity—the four concurrent outside posts began with him.

sentences.zh: 宋人請和。

translations.literal: Song requested peace.
translations.idiomatic: Song sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 賜銀五十兩、重彩十端。

translations.literal: He was given fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: He received fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy silk.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複侍講學士，兼諫議、修史、知審官院，轉侍讀，兼兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; on resumption he was Academician for Lectures with concurrent Remonstrator, history compiler, and head of the Bureau of Review, then Academician for Reading with concurrent Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned as Lectures Academician with remonstrance, history, and Bureau of Review duties, then Reading Academician and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，胡沙虎請廢衛紹王為庶人，思忠與奧屯忠孝阿附胡沙虎，曰：「竊人之財，猶謂之盜，況偷天位以私己乎！」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, Hushahu asked to demote Prince Shao of Wei to commoner status; Sizhong and Aotun Zhongxiao sided with Hushahu and said: "To steal another's goods is still called theft—how much more stealing the heavenly throne for oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou, Hushahu sought to demote Prince Shao of Wei; Sizhong and Aotun Zhongxiao backed him, saying: "Stealing another's goods is theft—how much more seizing the throne for oneself?"

sentences.zh: 宣宗不從。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷太子太保兼侍讀、修國史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with concurrent Academician for Reading and Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Reading Academician, and national history compiler.

sentences.zh: 二年春，享於太廟，思忠攝太尉，醉毆禮直官，御史台劾奏，降秘書監兼同修國史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he assisted at the Ancestral Temple; Sizhong acted as Grand Marshal, drunk beat the ritual officer, and the Censorate impeached him; he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year he assisted at the Ancestral Temple as acting Grand Marshal, beat a ritual officer while drunk, was impeached, and demoted to Secretariat Director while keeping national history work.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷翰林學士同修國史，卒。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Hanlin Academician and Compiler of the National History and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Hanlin Academician and national history compiler, then died.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈胡失門

translations.literal: Geshilie Husimen
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Husimen

sentences.zh: 完顏宇

translations.literal: Wanyan Yu
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Yu

sentences.zh: 完顏宇，本名訛出，西南路猛安人。

translations.literal: Wanyan Yu, original name Echu, was a native of a meng'an on the Southwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Yu, born Echu, came from a Southwest Route meng'an.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年進士，累調河東北路提刑司知事，改同知遼州軍州事，召為國史院編修官，遷應奉翰林文字、南京路轉運副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Dading he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred to Clerk of the Hedong North Route Judicial Commission, changed to Associate Prefect of Liaozhou, summoned as Compiler in the Institute for National History, transferred to Hanlin Academician for Service and Vice Transport Commissioner of the Nanjing Route.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-eighth year of Dading, served the Hedong North Route Judicial Commission, became Associate Prefect of Liaozhou, a national history compiler, Hanlin Academician for Service, and Nanjing Route Vice Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複太府監丞，改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; on resumption he was Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse Directorate and changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he returned as Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse and then Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大安初，除知登聞檢院，累遷右司郎中、翰林待制，兼侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was made Director of the Petition Inspection Court and rose through posts to Right Department Director, Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Da'an he directed the Petition Inspection Court, then became Right Department Director, Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, and Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，議衛紹王事，語在《衛紹王紀》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, when Prince Shao of Wei was discussed, the account is in the Annals of Prince Shao of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou, in the affair of Prince Shao of Wei, the account appears in his annals.

sentences.zh: 中都圍急，詔于東華門置招賢所，內外士庶皆得言事，或不次除官，由是閭閻細民，往往炫鬻求售。

translations.literal: When Zhongdu was besieged in grave peril, an edict set up a Talent Recruitment Office at the Donghua Gate; scholars and commoners inside and outside might all speak on affairs, and some received office out of turn; thus humble folk in the lanes often boasted and sold themselves for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongdu was besieged, a Talent Recruitment Office opened at Donghua Gate; anyone might speak and some won sudden office, so commoners boasted and sold advice.

sentences.zh: 王守信者，本一村夫，敢為大言，以諸葛亮為不知兵，宇薦於朝。

translations.literal: Wang Shouxin was originally a village man who dared big talk, saying Zhuge Liang did not understand war; Yu recommended him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouxin, a village man who claimed Zhuge Liang knew nothing of war, was recommended by Yu.

sentences.zh: 詔署行軍都統，募市井無賴為兵，教閱進退跳擲，大概似童戲。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Commander on Campaign, recruiting market riffraff as soldiers and drilling advance, retreat, leaping, and vaulting—altogether like children's games.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Commander on Campaign, raised market rabble as troops, and drilled them in leaps and marches like child's play.

sentences.zh: 其陣法大書「古今相對」四字於旗上，作黃布袍、緇巾、鑞牌各三十六事，牛頭響環六十四枚，欲以怖敵而走之，大率皆誕妄。

translations.literal: His formation banners bore the four characters "ancient and modern opposed"; he made thirty-six yellow robes, black headcloths, and tin plates, and sixty-four ox-head ringing chains to frighten the enemy into flight—all mostly absurd.
translations.idiomatic: His flags read "ancient versus modern"; he issued yellow robes, black caps, tin plates, and ox-head rattles to scare the enemy—all absurd.

sentences.zh: 因與其眾出城，殺百姓之樵采者以為功。

translations.literal: He then led his crowd outside the walls and killed townspeople gathering firewood to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men out and killed firewood gatherers to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 賈耐兒者，本歧路小說人，俚語詼嘲以取衣食，制運糧車千兩。

translations.literal: Jia Nai'er was originally a crossroads storyteller who earned food with rustic jokes and devised a thousand grain transport carts.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Nai'er, a street storyteller who lived on coarse wit, designed a thousand grain carts.

sentences.zh: 是時材木甚艱，所費浩大，觀者皆竊笑之。

translations.literal: Timber was then very scarce and the expense vast; onlookers all secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Timber was scarce and the cost huge; onlookers laughed.

sentences.zh: 草澤李棟在衛紹王時嘗事司天監李天惠，依附天文，假託占卜，趨走貴臣，俱為司天官。

translations.literal: Li Dong of the wilds had once served the Astronomical Directorate under Li Tianhui in Prince Shao of Wei's time; clinging to astronomy he feigned divination, hurried after great ministers, and all became Astronomical Directorate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dong, a rustic who had served the Astronomical Directorate under Li Tianhui for Prince Shao of Wei, clung to astronomy, feigned divination, courted great ministers, and all became directorate officials.

sentences.zh: 棟嘗密奏白氣貫紫微，主京師兵亂，幸不貫徹，得不成禍。

translations.literal: Dong once secretly memorialized that white vapor pierced the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, presaging military chaos in the capital; fortunately it did not run through and disaster did not form.
translations.idiomatic: Dong secretly reported white vapor crossing the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, foretelling capital revolt; it did not pierce through, so calamity failed to form.

sentences.zh: 既而高琪殺胡沙虎，宣宗愈益信之。

translations.literal: Afterward Gao Qi killed Hushahu and the Xuanzong Emperor trusted him still more.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Qi killed Hushahu, the Xuanzong Emperor trusted Dong all the more.

sentences.zh: 左諫議大夫張行信奏曰：「狂子庸流，猥蒙拔擢，參預機務，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrator Zhang Xingxin memorialized: "Madmen and vulgar streams are rashly promoted to join in great affairs—this is quite pointless.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrator Zhang Xingxin said: "Madmen and riffraff are promoted into state affairs—this is absurd.

sentences.zh: 司天之官，占見天象，據經陳奏，使人主飭已修政，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Astronomical officials observe the heavens, report according to the classics, and let the ruler restrain himself and repair government to turn misfortune to blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers read heaven by the classics so the ruler may reform and turn ill fortune to good.

sentences.zh: 如有天象，乞令諸監官公同陳奏，所見或異，則各以狀聞，不宜偏聽也。」

translations.literal: If there is a celestial sign, I beg that all directorate officials report together; if their views differ, each should state it in a memorial—not listen to one side alone."
translations.idiomatic: When signs appear, let all directorate officials report together; if views differ, each should memorialize separately—not hear one voice alone."

sentences.zh: 上召行信與宇面計守信事，複與近侍就決于高琪。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xingxin and Yu to discuss Shouxin face to face, then again decided with close attendants through Gao Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhang and Yu to discuss Shouxin, then consulted Gao Qi through close attendants.

sentences.zh: 高琪言守信不可用，上乃以行信之言為然。

translations.literal: Gao Qi said Shouxin could not be used; the emperor then took Xingxin's words as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi said Shouxin was useless; the emperor sided with Zhang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，宇遷禮部侍郎，改東京副留守、隴州防禦使，遷安化軍節度使，兼山東路統軍副使。

translations.literal: Shortly Yu was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, changed to Associate Defender of Dongjing and Defender of Longzhou, transferred to Military Commissioner of the Anhua Army with concurrent Vice Commander of the Shandong Route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu became Vice Minister of Rites, Associate Defender of Dongjing, Defender of Longzhou, Military Commissioner of the Anhua Army, and Shandong Route Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 興定元年四月，詔宇以本官權元帥左都監，行元帥府事，和輯苗道潤、移剌鐵哥軍事，語在道潤傳。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Xingding, an edict ordered Yu in his present post to act as Left Commander of the Marshal's Headquarters, directing marshal affairs, and reconciling the armies of Miao Daorun and Yila Tiege—the account is in Daorun's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Xingding, Yu was ordered to act as Left Marshal Commander, run headquarters affairs, and reconcile Miao Daorun and Yila Tiege—as told in Daorun's biography.

sentences.zh: 十二月，密州破，宇為亂軍所殺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Mizhou fell and Yu was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Mizhou fell and mutinous troops killed Yu.

sentences.zh: 斡勒合打

translations.literal: Wolei Heda
translations.idiomatic: Wolei Heda

sentences.zh: 斡勒合打，蓋州本得山猛安人。

translations.literal: Wolei Heda was a native of Bendeshan Meng'an in Gaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wolei Heda came from Bendeshan Meng'an in Gaizhou.

sentences.zh: 以廕補官，充親軍，調山陰尉。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he entered office, served in the Imperial Guard, and was appointed Wei of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he entered service, joined the Imperial Guard, and became Wei of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 縣當兵沖，合打率土豪官兵身先行陣。

translations.literal: The county lay on a military thoroughfare; Heda led local strongmen and official troops in person at the front of the formation.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay on a military route; Heda led local strongmen and troops at the front.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，以功遷本縣令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, for merit he was transferred to Magistrate of his county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he was promoted to magistrate of his county for merit.

sentences.zh: 縣升為忠州，合打充刺史。

translations.literal: When the county was raised to Zhong Prefecture, Heda served as its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the county became Zhong Prefecture, Heda became prefect.

sentences.zh: 州被兵久，耕桑俱廢，詔徙其民於太和嶺南。

translations.literal: The prefecture had long suffered warfare and farming and sericulture were both ruined; an edict moved its people south of Taihe Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: War had ruined farming and sericulture; the court moved the people south of Taihe Ridge.

sentences.zh: 合打遙授同知太原府事，仍領其眾。

translations.literal: Heda was given honorary appointment as Associate Prefect of Taiyuan Prefecture and still led his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Heda was made honorary Associate Prefect of Taiyuan while still leading his followers.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官遙授彰國軍節度使，權河東北路宣撫副使，督糧餉往代州。

translations.literal: Shortly with his present title he was given honorary appointment as Military Commissioner of the Zhangguo Army and acting Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Hedong North Route, supervising grain and fodder to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was honorary Military Commissioner of the Zhangguo Army and acting Hedong North Vice Pacification Commissioner, shipping grain to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 合打不欲行，因與宣撫使完顏伯嘉爭辨。

translations.literal: Heda did not wish to go and quarreled with Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Bojia.
translations.idiomatic: Heda refused to go and quarreled with Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Bojia.

sentences.zh: 合打恐伯嘉奏聞，乃先奏伯嘉辱己。

translations.literal: Fearing Bojia would memorialize, he first memorialized that Bojia had insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Bojia would report him, he accused Bojia of insulting him first.

sentences.zh: 御史台廉得其事，未及奏，伯嘉、合打皆改遷。

translations.literal: The Censorate investigated and learned the truth; before they could memorialize, both Bojia and Heda were transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate learned the truth; before reporting, both men were transferred.

sentences.zh: 合打改武甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: Heda was changed to Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Heda became Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 數月，召為勸農使。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned as Agricultural Encouragement Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was summoned as Agricultural Encouragement Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，為金安軍節度使。

translations.literal: After some time he was Military Commissioner of the Jin'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Military Commissioner of the Jin'an Army.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，複為勸農使，曆知河間府，權元帥右都監，行元帥府事，駐兵蔡、息間。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he again became Agricultural Encouragement Commissioner, served in succession as Administrator of Hejian Prefecture, acting Right Commander of the Marshal's Headquarters directing marshal affairs, and stationed troops between Cai and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding he again encouraged agriculture, governed Hejian, acted as Right Marshal Commander, and stationed troops between Cai and Xi.

sentences.zh: 權同簽樞密院事，守河清，改知歸德府事。

translations.literal: He acted as signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, held Heqing, and was changed to Administrator of Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, held Heqing, then governed Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 合打屢守邊要，無他將略，雖未嘗敗北，亦無大功。

translations.literal: Heda repeatedly held frontier posts but had no other military stratagem; though he never suffered defeat, he also won no great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Heda held many frontier posts without real strategy; he was never routed, yet won no great victories.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 蒲察移剌都

translations.literal: Puchayiladou
translations.idiomatic: Puchayiladou

sentences.zh: 蒲察移剌都，東京猛安人。

translations.literal: Puchayiladou was a native of a meng'an in Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Puchayiladou came from a meng'an in Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 父吾迭，太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: His father Wudie was Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wudie had retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 移剌都勇健多力，充護衛十人長，調同知秦州防禦使事、武衛軍鈐轄，以憂去官。

translations.literal: Yiladou was brave and strong; he served as chief of a ten-man guard unit, was appointed Associate Defender of Qinzhou and Commander of the Imperial Guard, and left office in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yiladou was strong and brave, led a ten-man guard unit, became Associate Defender of Qinzhou and Imperial Guard commander, then left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起複武器署令。

translations.literal: On resumption he was Director of the Weapons Office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he directed the Weapons Office.

sentences.zh: 從軍，兵潰被執。

translations.literal: He followed the army; when the troops were routed he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign his unit was routed and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，與降兵萬餘人俱脫歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he escaped back with more than ten thousand surrendered troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he escaped with more than ten thousand surrendered troops.

sentences.zh: 遷隆安府治中，賜銀百兩，重幣六端，遙授信州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrative Assistant of Long'an Prefecture, given a hundred taels of silver and six bolts of heavy silk, and made Prefect of Xin on honorary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He became Administrative Assistant of Long'an, received a hundred taels of silver and six bolts of heavy silk, and was made honorary Prefect of Xin.

sentences.zh: 有功，遷蒲與路節度使兼同知上京留守事，進三階，改知隆安府事。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Puyu Route with concurrent Associate Defender of the Shangjing Garrison, advanced three ranks, and changed to Administrator of Long'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became Military Commissioner of the Puyu Route and Associate Shangjing Defender, advanced three ranks, then governed Long'an.

sentences.zh: 逾年，充遼東、上京等路宣撫使兼左副元帥。

translations.literal: After more than a year he served as Pacification Commissioner of Liaodong, Shangjing, and other routes with concurrent Left Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he pacified Liaodong and Shangjing routes as Left Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 再閱月，就拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: After another month he was appointed Right Vice Chancellor on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made Right Vice Chancellor on the spot.

sentences.zh: 移剌都與上京行省蒲察五斤爭權，及賣隆安戰馬，擅造銀牌，睚眥殺人，已而矯稱宣召，棄隆安赴南京，宣宗皆釋不問。

translations.literal: Yiladou contended for power with the Shangjing Pacification Commission's Pucha Wujin, sold Long'an war horses, privately forged silver tallies, killed over petty grudges, then falsely claimed an imperial summons, abandoned Long'an for Nanjing—the Xuanzong Emperor released all without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Pucha Wujin of Shangjing for power, sold Long'an war horses, forged silver tallies, killed over slights, then falsely claimed an imperial summons and fled to Nanjing—the emperor forgave all.

sentences.zh: 除知河南府事，俄改元帥左監軍，權左副元帥，充陝西行省參議官。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Henan Prefecture, shortly changed to Left Marshal Supervisor with acting Left Vice Marshal and Councilor of the Shaanxi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Henan Prefecture, then became Left Marshal Supervisor, acting Left Vice Marshal, and Shaanxi Pacification Councilor.

sentences.zh: 無何，兼陝西路統軍使。

translations.literal: Before long he also commanded the Shaanxi Route army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also commanded the Shaanxi Route army.

sentences.zh: 興定二年四月，改簽樞密院事，權右副元帥，行樞密院于鄧州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Xingding he was changed to signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, acting Right Vice Marshal, directing the mobile bureau from Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Xingding he signed the Bureau of Military Affairs, acted as Right Vice Marshal, and ran the mobile bureau from Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史台奏移剌都在軍中，買沙覆道，盜用官銀，矯制收禁書，指斥鑾輿，使親軍守門，護衛押宿，擬前後衛仗，婢妾效內人妝飾等數事。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized that in the army Yiladou bought sand to cover roads, embezzled official silver, forged edicts to seize and ban books, insulted the imperial carriage, made his personal guard hold gates, had guards escort him overnight, imitated front and rear imperial guards, and had concubines dress like palace women, among several matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate charged that in camp he bought sand for roads, embezzled silver, forged edicts to ban books, insulted the throne, used personal guards as gatekeepers, posted escorts overnight, imitated imperial guards, and dressed concubines as palace women.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部尚書阿不罕斜不失鞫之，坐是誅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Personnel Abuhan Xiebushi to interrogate him; for this he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Abuhan Xiebushi was ordered to try him; he was executed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：讀《金史》，至張行信論奧屯忠孝事，曰：嗟乎，宣宗之不足與有為也如此！

translations.literal: The encomium says: Reading the History of Jin, when one reaches Zhang Xingxin's discussion of Aotun Zhongxiao, one sighs: Alas, the Xuanzong Emperor was insufficient for great action to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Reading the History of Jin at Zhang Xingxin's attack on Aotun Zhongxiao, one sighs that the Xuanzong Emperor was unfit for great deeds.

sentences.zh: 夫進退宰執，豈無其道也哉！

translations.literal: Advancing and retiring chancellors—is there not a proper way?
translations.idiomatic: Surely there is a proper way to advance and retire chancellors.

sentences.zh: 語其親知，諷之求去，豈禮邪？

translations.literal: To tell his close friends and hint that he should seek to leave—is that ritual?
translations.idiomatic: To tell his friends to hint resignation—is that ritual conduct?

sentences.zh: 是故奧屯忠孝、蒲察思忠之黨比，紇石烈胡失門之疲眾，完顏宇之輕信誤國，斡勒合打之詆訟上官，於是曾不之罪，失政刑矣，豈小懲大誡之道哉！

translations.literal: Thus the faction of Aotun Zhongxiao and Pucha Sizhong, the weary troops of Geshilie Husimen, the credulous Wanyan Yu who misled the state, and Wolei Heda who slandered his superiors were none punished; government and punishments failed—is this the way of small warning and great admonition?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the faction of Aotun Zhongxiao and Pucha Sizhong, Geshilie Husimen's exhausted troops, Wanyan Yu's credulity that misled the state, and Wolei Heda's slanders against superiors went unpunished—government and punishment collapsed. Is that how small faults should warn and great ones chastise?
